title: Understanding the VPS 5 Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion Guide
description: Learn how to convert a VPS 5 salary from hourly to annual using the 38-hour week, plus tax, super, and Fair Work Ombudsman rates.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary for a VPS 5 role?
faqs.a: Use the standard formula: annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For full-time VPS roles, assume 38 hours per week. If you have a casual loading (25% on top), add that before multiplying. Remember that superannuation (12% from 1 July 2026) is paid on top of your ordinary earnings, not deducted from the annual figure.

faqs.q: Does the VPS 5 salary include super and how is tax calculated?

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting an Hourly Rate to an Annual Salary

When you’re offered a job or considering a pay rise, understanding how an hourly rate translates to an annual salary is essential. The standard formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For full-time roles in Australia, the typical week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This means the annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, if your hourly rate is $30, your annual gross would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It’s a useful baseline, but your actual take-home pay will differ after tax and super.

## The VPS 5 Salary in Context

The term “VPS 5 salary” refers to a classification in the Victorian Public Service. While the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/) cover minimum award rates, VPS 5 is typically above those minimums. To compare a VPS 5 hourly offer with an annual figure, use the same 38-hour week assumption. For instance, a VPS 5 hourly rate of $55 gives an annual gross of $108,680. Always verify the exact salary against the current VPS enterprise agreement, as rates are reviewed periodically.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making their minimum $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and apply to employees not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. Most VPS roles are covered by an award, so your rate should be at least the relevant award rate, which is often higher than the minimum. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) to check the correct classification.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you’re a casual employee, your hourly rate typically includes a 25% casual loading. When converting to annual, apply the loading first. For example, a base rate of $30 becomes $37.50 with loading, then annual gross = $37.50 × 38 × 52 = $74,100. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means your employer adds super to your gross pay, not deducts it. For more details, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27: no tax on the first $18,200, then 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy adds 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). For a VPS 5 salary of $108,680, the tax would be approximately $24,000 plus Medicare, leaving a take-home pay of around $82,000. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

## Fortnightly and Weekly Breakdown

It’s also helpful to see your pay on a fortnightly basis. A fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For a $30 hourly rate, weekly is $1,140, fortnightly $2,280. This can help with budgeting. The [reference tables](/blog). This is a broader measure. A VPS 5 salary often sits around the median. The Fair Work Ombudsman reminds that annualised wages must be reviewed annually to ensure no underpayment.

## Summary

Converting an hourly rate to annual is simple: multiply by 38 and 52. For a VPS 5 salary, use that formula, then add super on top. Always check your award or agreement. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool for quick calculations.
